hero: In a bright outpatient clinic in Batangas, a Filipino pediatric nephrologist measures a tall 12-year-old Filipino boy in a basketball jersey against a wall stadiometer while his mother holds a growth chart; a pediatric blood pressure cuff set hangs on the wall, friendly and focused mood, no text.

figures.teaches: The same creatinine means different kidney function depending on muscle mass.
figures.content: Three child silhouettes side by side, each with the same lab tag 'Creatinine same'. Left: muscular athlete, label 'More muscle', arrow 'eGFR falsely low', note 'Add cystatin C'. Middle: average child, label 'Typical muscle', note 'Equation fits'. Right: thin child in wheelchair, label 'Little muscle', arrow 'eGFR falsely high', note 'Use cystatin C'. Footer formula: 'Bedside Schwartz: 0.413 × height (cm) / creatinine (mg/dL)'.

figures.teaches: A referral becomes a problem statement in five steps.
figures.content: Five boxes top to bottom with arrows: 1 'Who is the child' (age, height, muscle, supplements); 2 'Is the number real' (rest, right cuff, first-morning urine); 3 'Estimate properly' (validated equation, cystatin C); 4 'Look for company' (BP, urine, growth); 5 'Write it' (one quantified sentence). Side icon of a growth chart labeled 'Growth is a vital sign'.

card: A pediatric nephrologist holding a growth chart beside a young athlete in a clinic, no text.
